dependency_edges.handoff: Cited density-speed behavior motivates speed as an output but does not define the final evaluator.
Class-dependent safe intervals feed the movement branches.
Cell geometry and state receive generated vehicles and support movement.
Cell occupancy and completions feed passing time, velocity and variance criteria.
Dual-Gaussian hourly density replaces uniform arrivals in the time-based run.
Basic cellular trajectories feed autonomous-share comparisons.
Velocity and two variances supply network scenario metrics.
Peak timing defines the 17:00 and peak-hour comparisons.
The same movement model is rerun after lane-access changes.
Average velocity and space variance compare lane policies.
Network share results provide the no-dedication baseline.
Adverse lane results identify new lane-count and route-response scenarios for later network runs.
